approved: Crimes Legislation Amendment (Police Powers at Airports) Bill 2018
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would give police and protective service officers new powers at major airports.
They could direct people to show identification, leave the airport, or not take a flight for up to 24 hours.
An identity check direction could be issued if the officer suspects a person has committed an offence punishable by 12 months or more imprisonment, or considers it necessary for aviation security.
Creates identity check, move-on and ancillary directions at major airports.
Allows the relevant Minister to determine which airports the new powers apply to.
Introduces offences for failing to comply with a direction.
Constables and protective service officers at major airports, and people at those airports.

The government introduced the Crimes Legislation Amendment (Police Powers at Airports) Bill to expand police powers at major airports, enabling identity checks without requiring suspicion of an offence and allowing 24-hour move-on directions to disrupt serious crime and security threats, following a disrupted terrorist plot targeting a Sydney flight in July. The bill creates new offences for non-compliance with fines up to $4,200 and applies to all major capital city airports plus Gold Coast, Launceston, Alice Springs, Townsville, and Cairns.
